checks: The base-only tilt adds the same scalar to every vertex margin of one fiber, keeping all margin differences and hence the denominator constant. Finiteness and strict signs preserve all trace regimes locally.

Exactly one negative vertex makes the excluded portion a simplex cut on the d incident edges. Multiplying the positive intercept fractions gives (h_z-t delta a·(z-z_0))^d/D_z. Its negative second derivative gives the claimed sign and exponent d-2.

An off-anchor proper fiber supplies a direction with a nonzero scalar product. Every other proper term has the same weak sign and strictly saturated terms are zero, so first-order cancellation cannot restore a local minimum.
The original f2be43e7a9dbeca5 §3 has the same one-excluded strict regime. A triangle with a boundary vertex is not in the stated strict triangular specialization.

overlap.comparison: The accepted single-simplex Hessian allows this sign range when d>=2 but has no one-excluded base-tilt sign or off-anchor descent conclusion.

readability: The proper traces are assumed strict, so a vertex lying on a cap plane is outside this claim.
review_method: Independent cold proof read of frozen bytes, source locator audit, comparison to accepted and same-batch predecessors, and direct checks of the derivations.
summary: The excluded-simplex volume gives the exact second variation for a common base tilt and is strictly concave along a suitable line if a proper fiber lies off the anchor base.
